n: The converted Lamanite king issues a proclamation protecting Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and all their companions throughout his land.
The decree forbids binding, imprisoning, spitting on, beating, expelling, whipping, or stoning the missionaries — the very abuses they had suffered — and opens homes and places of worship to them.

The king, now converted with his household, wanted God’s word to spread unhindered so his people would see their fathers’ errors, recognize all as brothers, and stop murdering, stealing, and other sins.
Aaron and his brothers travel from city to city, establishing churches and ordaining priests and teachers among the Lamanites, with great success.
Thousands come to know the Lord and learn the Nephite records and prophecies.

f.w: thousands were brought to the knowledge of the Lord

n: A remarkable claim, stated with an oath: every Lamanite converted through these missionaries never fell away.
They laid down the weapons of their rebellion — no longer fighting God or their brothers.

f.g: Both literal weapons and spiritual rebellion.

n: Mormon now lists the converted peoples.

f.g: A roll of honor for the converted.

n: The Lamanites in the land of Ishmael — Lamoni’s kingdom.
The Lamanites in Middoni, where Aaron had been imprisoned.
The Lamanites in the city of Nephi, the high king’s capital.
Also those in Shilom, Shemlon, Lemuel, and Shimnilom — places once associated with Zeniff’s colony and its troubles.
All these were Lamanite cities whose converts laid down their weapons of war.
Only one Amalekite and no Amulonites converted. They hardened their own hearts and those of nearby Lamanites. The dissenters proved hardest of all.

f.g: Mormon notes even a single conversion.

n: Mormon has named every Lamanite city where people were converted.
The converts want a new name to set them apart, and the king consults Aaron and the priests.

f.w: that they might have a name

n: They choose “Anti-Nephi-Lehies” and are no longer called Lamanites. The name’s meaning is uncertain; it seems to honor both Nephi and Lehi, perhaps also recalling the king’s son of the same name.

f.g: “Anti” here is not the English prefix; some suggest it may relate to a word meaning “facing” or “of.”

n: They become hardworking, befriend the Nephites, and open communication with them; the curse of God no longer follows them.

f.w: the curse of God did no more follow them

f.g: Hardworking — a reversal of the idleness described in Alma 17:15.
